subtopic: Process Signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL), Zombies and Orphan Reaping
question_text: [Linux System Administration & Shell Scripting - Q31] When a process PID 1 inside a Docker container runs an application directly without an init system (like `tini`), why can orphan child processes cause container instability?

options.text: Linux relies on PID 1 to reap terminated orphan zombie processes; standard applications do not handle `waitpid()`, leading to zombie accumulation and PID exhaustion
Containers crash if any child process terminates
Orphans bypass container cgroup memory limits

answer_explanation: PID 1 is responsible for reaping adopted orphan processes. Standard application binaries (e.g. Node, Python) do not register SIGCHLD handlers to reap zombies, causing PID table exhaustion.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: PID 1 is responsible for reaping adopted orphan processes. Standard application binaries (e.g. Node, Python) do not register SIGCHLD handlers to reap zombies, causing PID table exhaustion.
